question: Which system of India is based on the Westminster model?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Parliamentary system**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Parliamentary system** is based on the Westminster model.
 
• The Westminster model is a democratic parliamentary system of government modeled after the politics of the United Kingdom.
 
• It features a head of state, who is different from the head of government, and a parliament with two houses.
 
• In India, the President is the head of state, while the Prime Minister is the head of government.
 
• The Indian Parliament consists of two houses: the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• This system emphasizes the role of the Prime Minister and the Cabinet, who are accountable to the Lok Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Westminster model** originated in the United Kingdom and has been adopted by various countries, including India, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.
 
• The Indian Constitution was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, which was heavily influenced by the British system of governance.
 
• The Indian Parliamentary system ensures a separation of powers among the executive, legislative, and judicial branches of government.
 
• The system also incorporates a series of checks and balances to prevent any one branch from becoming too powerful.
 
• The Prime Minister and the Cabinet are collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, which reflects the principle of collective responsibility.
